newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian forex market inactive on bank staff strike.
newsitem.headline: Indian forex market inactive on bank staff strike.

text.p: * India's inter-bank forex market was virtually shut on Friday as bank employees across the country began a one-day strike, dealers say.
* No banks quoting prices even after the market's opening hours. State Bank of India (SBI) and other state-run banks, closed because of the strike, they say.
* Some back-office staff join the strike at some foreign banks. "The market is virtually closed today. There could be some stray deals by foreign banks," says a chief dealer.
* The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) told banks on Thursday it is open and ready to facilitate operations but this would not help as banks staff abstain from work, a dealer says.

The rupee opened steady against the dollar at 35.76/77 on Friday, dealers said. The quotes were delayed and restricted to a handful of foreign banks as state-run Indian banks are virtually shut on Friday because of a countrywide strike.
"These are just quotes, there are no deals," said a dealer.

The rupee moved up against the dollar on Thursday in the absence of demand from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the State Bank of India (SBI), India's leading commercial bank and traditionally the largest dollar buyer in the market.
On Thursday, the rupee traded at a high of 35.7675 and a low of 35.7925, with most of the day's trade between 35.775 and 35.785.
"Apart from the strike, we heard there's a 'bandh' (general strike) in West Bengal," said a foreign bank's chief dealer.
Some 1.3 million bank employees across the nation are striking to protest government's plan to allow private banks to set up operations in rural areas, trade union officials said.
